diagnosis.summary: The farmer in Kakamega is harvesting small-sized Irish potatoes instead of normal, marketable tubers.
likely_causes: Using recycled seeds from previous harvests which carry viruses that stunt tuber growth.
Low soil nutrients and high soil acidity which are common in the Kakamega region.
Poor earthing up and tight spacing which limit the physical space for tubers to expand.
diagnosis.recommended_approach: Apply plenty of well-rotted animal manure to improve soil fertility, space plants properly, and try to obtain clean certified seeds for the next season.

this_week_actions: Measure and mark your planting rows to ensure a spacing of 30 centimeters between plants and 75 centimeters between rows.
Dig planting furrows and mix in two handfuls of well-rotted animal manure per planting hole.
Earth up the soil around the base of existing potato plants to a height of 25 centimeters to give tubers space to grow.
Visit your nearest certified agrodealer to book disease-free certified potato seeds for your next planting.
materials_needed: Well-rotted dry cow or chicken manure from local livestock farmers.
A standard measuring tape or a pre-marked wooden stick to guide spacing.
A sturdy hand hoe for digging furrows and earthing up soil.
warning_signs: Leaves turning yellow, curling upward, or showing dark spots despite proper watering.
Stems wilting suddenly during the day and rotting at the base with a foul smell.
action_plan.expected_outcome: You will harvest larger, more marketable potato tubers by the end of the next harvesting season in about four months.
